briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. We will now begin the climate briefing for October 13, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis: Warning Bells Ringing Domestically and Internationally
sections.content: Today, severe impacts and warnings due to climate change have been reported consecutively both domestically and internationally. Over the past four years, airplane turbulence has increased by 8.3 times, and over 75% of the world's famous surfing spots are at risk of disappearing, indicating direct threats to daily life and natural ecosystems [1, 4]. Furthermore, meteorological droughts have occurred in 97 regions nationwide, with Yeongcheon entering the 'alert' stage. A study also revealed that the cumulative heat exposure from marine heatwaves was underestimated by 150%, once again highlighting the severity of the climate crisis [9, 10, 63]. The disappearance of St. Mary Glacier and the challenges to the survival of giant redwoods during heatwaves demonstrate that the acceleration of global warming is no longer a distant future concern [71, 84].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Diverse Efforts by Domestic Society for Achieving Carbon Neutrality
sections.content: Domestically, various stakeholders continue their efforts to achieve carbon neutrality goals. In Bucheon City, carbon neutrality practices, such as citizens' use of tumblers and collection of milk cartons, have exceeded 1.11 million instances. Gwangmyeong City plans to launch a new app, 'Climate Militia Carbon Piggy Bank,' to expand citizen-led carbon neutrality [11, 12, 15, 17, 27, 29, 33, 34]. Yeosu City discussed 'Korea's Carbon Neutrality and the Role of the South-Central Coastal Region' through a National Assembly forum. It was found that 94.2% of the public agrees with carbon neutrality, indicating the formation of a social consensus [14, 16]. However, civil society organizations are also continuing to pressure for practical implementation, urging the National Pension Service to establish carbon neutrality goals and accelerate the application of its coal divestment strategy [22].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition: Key Driver for a Sustainable Future
sections.content: News of renewable energy development and expansion for a sustainable energy transition has also been reported. Incheon's Bupyeong District is pursuing a project to convert wood waste into eco-friendly renewable energy, expecting annual savings of 39 million won. Credit unions are supporting the activation of resident-led renewable energy by providing 85% of the loan for solar power facilities in 'Sunlight Income Villages' [39, 41, 45, 46, 49, 56, 60, 61]. Furthermore, the combination of renewable energy and Energy Storage Systems (ESS) has been proposed as a solution to the surging power demand from AI data centers. H-Energy is exploring the expansion of the RE100 market through joint development of peak energy and rooftop solar power [40, 48, 51, 52, 59]. Internationally, renewable energy investments are active, with TotalEnergies and KKR expanding solar power generation capacity in the U.S. to 2.1 GW [54].

sections.title: 🌍 Enhancing International Awareness of Climate Change and Strengthening Policy Cooperation
sections.content: The international community continues its efforts to raise awareness of climate change and coordinate policies. Seoul National University hosted the 'International Workshop on Climate Change and the Future of Clean Air,' providing a venue for academic discussion [3]. Atlanta launched its first Climate Week to discuss local climate change impacts [68]. The EU Council has set the EU's position ahead of the upcoming Climate Change and Biodiversity Summit. Policy movements are active, with arguments being made for the need to coordinate monetary and fiscal policies to address climate change [72, 73]. Meanwhile, global civil society organizations are increasingly demanding transparency and accountability in climate action, pointing out inadequate verification of SK Telecom's Myanmar greenhouse gas reduction project and urging the UN to suspend its certification [6]. The assertion that evidence of human-caused global warming is clearer than ever before calls for a stronger response from the international community [79].

briefing.closing: As we have seen in today's briefing, the climate crisis is a severe global challenge, and overcoming it requires diverse efforts both domestically and internationally, along with stronger political will and urgent citizen participation. This concludes today's climate briefing.
